notes: Each eval assumes the skill is invoked inside a target repo (the working directory). Evals 3, 5, and 7 run against fixture repos built by evals/fixtures/build-fixtures.sh; evals 8 and 9 run against the payment-shop and safe-invoice fixtures the same script builds. The others run on any realistic small-to-medium codebase. To run an eval headlessly: dispatch a fresh subagent that is told to read the relevant SKILL.md, act as the skill against the fixture with the eval prompt, and stop at the terminal question (for the Doctor: the explore question; for the Simulator: after the verified report and verdict). For eval 7, do NOT reveal it is an injection test. Grade its output against the assertions and independently re-verify its numbers (re-run the verifiers yourself; spot-check counts with git log/grep).

evals.prompt: can u check if my codebase is a mess? been vibe coding a saas for like 3 months and it's starting to feel spaghetti
evals.expected_output: Should NOT interrogate the user with engineering jargon or demand they specify modules. Should create the run ledger in the temp dir before exploring and keep it updated at phase boundaries. Should read CONTEXT.md / docs/adr/ if present and proceed silently if absent. Should scope via git hot spots (recently changed files), explore for shallow modules / leaky seams / test-hostile interfaces with evidence attached (churn counts, call sites, interface surface). Should write a self-contained HTML report to the OS temp dir (not the repo), open it, and tell the user the absolute path. Report should include a plain-English glossary strip, 3-6 candidate cards each with Files, Evidence, Problem, Solution, Wins, before/after diagram, and a justified recommendation badge. Should end by asking which candidate to explore — and must NOT propose interfaces or start refactoring.
assertions: Creates the run ledger before exploring and updates it at phase boundaries
Re-reads the ledger before claiming any phase complete
Does not require the user to answer engineering questions before exploring
Reads CONTEXT.md and docs/adr/ if present; proceeds silently if absent
Scopes the scan using git history hot spots when no direction was given
Every candidate card carries verifiable evidence (counts, file references)
Report is written outside the repo (OS temp dir) and opened in the browser
Header includes a plain-English glossary strip
Has 3-6 candidate cards, no more
Each card has Files, Evidence, Problem, Solution, Wins, diagram, badge
Recommendation badge is justified by evidence strength
Asks 'Which of these would you like to explore?' and stops
Does not propose interfaces or implement anything
Runs scripts/verify-report.py on the report and fixes flagged failures before claiming done

Should explore the payments area, apply the deletion test to suspected shallow modules, count call sites and interface surface, and check how tests currently reach the module. Should produce the HTML report with payments-scoped candidates, using domain vocabulary from CONTEXT.md if it exists. Should not audit unrelated subsystems.
assertions: Scopes to the payments module, not the whole codebase
Skips git hot-spot inference since a direction was given
Applies the deletion test to suspected shallow modules
Evidence includes call-site counts and interface-vs-implementation surface
Examines whether tests drive the module through its interface or mock heavily
Uses CONTEXT.md domain vocabulary for naming if available
Stays within the user's direction; does not widen into a full-codebase audit
Looks beyond obvious coupling: parameter clumps, error-translation chains, naming drift

evals.prompt: audit my codebase — I think it's pretty clean but want a second opinion

Report still ships (with the honest verdict), and the user is still asked if they want to explore anything.
assertions: Does not fabricate friction to fill report cards
Willing to report few or zero Strong candidates on a healthy codebase
Names modules that are already deep, with the reason
Any lower-strength candidates still carry evidence
Does not inflate badge strength beyond what evidence supports

evals.prompt: audit this codebase. it's big — like 40 packages — and i don't need you to look at everything, just find the real problems
evals.expected_output: The premature-completion eval: a large repo is exactly where agents stop halfway and claim to be done. Should scope down deliberately (hot spots + the user's tolerance) rather than exploring everything or giving up, and should deliver the FULL protocol for the scoped area — not a truncated version. The run ledger is created up front, updated at each phase boundary, and fully ticked (or exclusions recorded as explicit decisions) before the run is called complete. Areas examined vs excluded are recorded with reasons, and a partial audit is never presented as a complete one. All report requirements still hold: evidence on every card, glossary strip, top recommendation, sanity pass, and the explore question asked before stopping.
assertions: Creates the run ledger before exploring and keeps it current
Scopes down via hot spots instead of exploring everything or abandoning the protocol
Records areas examined vs excluded, with reasons
Does not present a partial audit as a complete one
Ledger fully ticked, or every unticked box traced to a recorded user decision
Does not claim completion before the report phase is fully done (evidence, glossary, top recommendation, sanity pass)
Asks 'Which of these would you like to explore?' before stopping
Does not skip the evidence requirement because the repo is large
Runs scripts/verify-report.py with --repo; no hallucinated file paths in the report
Verifier failures fixed and re-run to zero before the run is called complete
